Subject: OpenPilot dedicated capacity validation - quick recap + targets

Thanks again for the call this morning — quick recap from our side and a few asks so we can kick off the pilot. High-level targets we discussed:

- 95th percentile end-to-end latency <= 120 ms for short prompts (avg 30-50 tokens).
- Streaming tail latency (first token + finalization) <= 300 ms 99th.
- Steady-state throughput target: 250 requests/sec with an average response length ~40 tokens.
- Concurrency observed in our traffic estimates: 30-60 simultaneous active requests (peaks at 80).

We covered caching behavior (many requests share the same prefix ~15% of traffic) and a mix of synchronous single-shot requests and streaming sessions. Primary risk for us is tail latency under bursty traffic and quantization quality when using 8-bit variants.

Requests:
1) Can you send a recommended GPU shortlist and a suggested reserved-throughput sizing that maps to the SLOs above? Include per-GPU expected RPS and recommended concurrency/batch settings.
2) Proposal for a validation pilot (duration, test plan, acceptance criteria). We prefer a 48–72 hour soak if possible.
3) We can share a 50k sample of production-like prompts; please confirm where to upload and any preferred formatting.

Attachments: openpilot-slo-matrix.xlsx (contains our target rows + sample percentiles)

Thanks — attaching Mike Turner, Sofia Ramos (platform) who will coordinate the data share./Mike

Quick plan (short):

- Pilot: 48-hour soak + targeted tail-latency stress windows (burst tests) + streaming tail validation.
- Acceptance: meet 95p latency <=120ms and streaming tail 99p <=300ms for >= 90% of test windows; regression tolerances specified in attached matrix.

Immediate asks for you: please upload the 50k prompt sample to the Drive link Aditya shared in chat (or reply here if you prefer a secure transfer). Also indicate which model variant you want us to test first (we recommended starting with your current production variant).

Preliminary GPU shortlist (high-level, more detail to follow in Karthik's note):
- H100-80GB (fp16 / q8) — best perf for high throughput + streaming, strong at long-context workloads.
- A100-40GB (fp16 / q4/q8) — good balance for mid-range throughput and cost.
- L40S / L40X (24-48GB) — cost-efficient for lower-latency single-shot but lower throughput per card.

Sizing sketch (very rough): to hit 250 rps with 40-token avg we estimate: 5x H100 OR 7x A100 OR ~14x L40S (these numbers are conservative initial guesses; Karthik will provide bench figures). Reserved-throughput policy: we can map to per-GPU throughput and add burst headroom (20–30%) with autoscale guardrails.

I'll attach a short pilot checklist and ask Karthik to follow with the micro-bench numbers and exact test commands.

Adding the micro-bench numbers and a simple sizing calc below. These are lab figures for the model family you described (short to mid responses, mostly ~40 tokens). We'll run them again with your 50k sample, but this gives a concrete starting point.

Bench assumptions: 40-token avg response, batch-friendly serializer, streaming enabled for responses. Numbers are steady-state RPS per GPU (95th-latency constrained):
- H100-80GB (fp16 / q8): ~60 RPS per GPU (95p<120ms observed in our lab for this workload).
- A100-40GB (fp16 / q8): ~42 RPS per GPU (95p ≈ 120–150ms depending on burst profile).
- L40S (24GB, q4/q8 mix): ~18 RPS per GPU (good p50/p90 but higher tail under burst).

Sizing for 250 RPS (steady-state target):
- H100 path: 250 / 60 = 4.2 => reserve 5 GPUs (reserve 5, allow 1 extra for bursts -> 6 total reserved with autoscale).
- A100 path: 250 / 42 = 5.95 => reserve 6 GPUs (7 with burst headroom).
- L40S path: 250 / 18 = 13.9 => reserve 14 GPUs (add 3 for headroom -> 17).

Streaming considerations: streaming sessions keep KV caches hot and increase memory footprint; for streaming-heavy fits we bias toward H100 since it sustains lower streaming tail. If a high fraction of traffic uses prefix caching we can reduce required GPUs by ~10–15% (depends on hit rate).

Test plan (short):
1) Throughput stability: run 6-hour steady-state at 85% of target (213 RPS) then 2 x 10-min bursts to 120% (300 RPS) while collecting 95/99 latencies.
2) Streaming tail: 4 x 30-min windows where we open 500 concurrent streaming sessions at client-patterned cadence, measure first-byte and finalization latencies.
3) Regression quality: run 2k sampled prompts through q4/q8 variants to check output drift and flag any >5% quality drop on eval metric.

Telemetry hooks we need: per-request trace id, token-level timestamps for first-token and final-token, model-variant tag, and KV-cache hit tag. We'll provide a small instrumentation snippet.

I attached a compact PDF with the per-GPU matrix and the test commands (dedicated-gpu-comparison.pdf).
